description: Machine-readable source of truth for the EngineOS router. One entry per row of CLAUDE.md's '| Intent (signals) | Load |' table, which stays the human mirror. scripts/validate-engineos.sh (C16) checks this file against CLAUDE.md (row count, drift alarm) and against registries/routing.json (every hook_mirrored intent carries a domain FK whose rules array matches the registry), and resolves every unqualified rule, skill and agent name to a file under rules/, skills/ and agents/. Plugin-qualified skill names (superpowers:*) and the external code-review skill are not resolved locally.

intents.title: New feature / multi-file change
intents.note: New behavior with no more-specific row below; a more specific matching row suppresses this one. brainstorming first, then writing-plans for spec/design/tasks, then whichever stack rows also match — so this row names no rules of its own. The brainstorm+plan workflow applies at non-negotiable #1's threshold (>2 files or any new feature); a small single-file tweak skips straight to the stack rules. Once tasks exist, always-on rules/parallelism.md dispatches independent tasks as parallel agents. model_tier is null because the tier is delegated to the brainstorm/plan flow and to the matched stack rows.

intents.title: Big / multi-domain / sweep work
intents.note: Both named rules are already always-on; the row names them to make the fan-out obligation explicit. Fan out via /engineos:implement <domain> <task> for changes, /engineos:audit for analysis, or N Task calls in ONE message over disjoint scopes. /engineos:implement dispatch is spec-gated. Tier is design: the row's primary work is fan-out planning and task decomposition, not the changes themselves.

intents.title: Bug / unexpected behavior
intents.note: Tier is design per registries/models.json work type hard-debugging.

intents.title: Backend work
intents.note: Rules follow registries/routing.json's order (the registry wins for this field); CLAUDE.md lists the same five rules in a different order, architecture first. data.md is loaded because the signals include migrations and nestjs-patterns defers migration safety to it; architecture.md and observability.md are closure targets of backend.md. The nestjs MCP is for codegen. backend-coordinator (alias borisenko) is dual-mode AUDIT/IMPLEMENT.

intents.title: Frontend work
intents.note: Rules follow registries/routing.json's order (the registry wins); CLAUDE.md lists the same three with architecture first. Must be matched after mobile in the hook chain, since mobile screens are .tsx too. frontend-coordinator alias arturo.

intents.title: Mobile work / mirror web to mobile
intents.note: Store build/publish requests belong to ios-release / android-release, not here. Rules follow registries/routing.json's order (the registry wins); CLAUDE.md lists the same five with architecture first. All of them are adapted the mobile way: frontend.md for component/state patterns, backend.md for the API-consumption parts, observability.md as backend.md's closure target; react-patterns is adapted to React Native. mobile-coordinator (alias elias) covers greenfield mobile features and web->mobile mirroring, treats the web frontend as read-only reference when mirroring, and writes only in the mobile tree — never API/backend, web frontend, or DevOps.

intents.title: Mobile store release — Apple
intents.note: CLAUDE.md carries a single 'Mobile store release' row; it is modelled as two intents here so that each keeps a 1:1 domain FK into registries/routing.json, which has separate ios-release and android-release domains. Full pipeline: preflight, version bump, quality gates, signed build, TestFlight upload. App Store review submission and production rollout happen only on explicit instruction. Always-on security.md governs signing keys and store credentials. Precedes mobile in the hook chain by matching only build/release files, so ordinary React Native screens fall through.

intents.title: Mobile store release — Google Play
intents.note: Second half of CLAUDE.md's single 'Mobile store release' row, split to keep a 1:1 domain FK into registries/routing.json. Full pipeline: preflight, version bump, quality gates, signed AAB, track upload. Production-track rollout only on explicit instruction. Always-on security.md governs the upload keystore and Play service-account key.

intents.title: LLM/agent work
intents.note: Last in the hook precedence chain. llm-coordinator alias hermsdorff. An LLM feature with no evals also matches the eval-setup row.

intents.title: DBA / data layer
intents.note: Rules follow registries/routing.json's order (the registry wins); CLAUDE.md lists architecture first. High floor: migrations are the canonical irreversible change. dba-coordinator (alias ronaldo) writes migrations and queries and holds NO database MCP; live schema and plan introspection is the read-only postgres-specialist / oracle-specialist leaves. routing.json names only dba-coordinator as the hook's agent — the two leaves are named by the CLAUDE.md row, so this array is a superset of the registry's single agent field.

intents.title: DevOps / infra
intents.note: High floor: infra config changes reach production by definition. devops-coordinator (alias hinokuma) writes config and holds NO cloud MCP; live cluster, cloud and CI introspection is the read-only kubernetes-specialist / gcp-specialist / cicd-specialist leaves. routing.json names only devops-coordinator as the hook's agent, so this array is a superset of the registry's single agent field.

intents.title: Editing security-sensitive files
intents.note: First in the hook precedence chain — cross-cutting, checked before every other domain, and delimiter-bounded so authors/ does not collide with auth/. security.md is already always-on; this row's real contribution is the security-reviewer dispatch (alias leo-ely), which is design tier per registries/models.json work type adversarial-review.

intents.title: System comprehension / onboarding docs
intents.note: Docs and onboarding output only — defect and health findings go to the audit row. architecture-analyst (alias analyst) runs patterns/1-Analysis.md and produces code-grounded architecture and onboarding docs.

intents.title: Fill doc gaps by interview
signals: ask me about how X works
intents.note: architecture-analyst in INTERVIEW mode (patterns/2-Interview-brainstorm.md). Interactive by design; folds the answers back into docs/. Not dispatchable non-interactively.

intents.title: End-to-end API QA
intents.note: qa-tester (alias qa): clean-slate Docker up, endpoint inventory JSON plus Postman collection, headless Newman run of all endpoints and scenarios (skips MFA and email steps), pass/fail report. Non-interactive — never waits for input.

intents.title: Multi-domain audit / system health check
intents.note: Read-only. Defect and health findings only; docs and onboarding output go to the system-comprehension row. The row names the command, not the agents: /engineos:audit <domain|all> fans out to the domain coordinators in AUDIT mode plus the read-only MCP leaf specialists, then consolidates via audit-consolidator (alias corradin) into a status report. agents is empty on purpose so this entry stays a faithful mirror of the table cell.

intents.title: Refactor / cleanup
intents.note: Finish with an explicit simplify pass over the diff: dead code, one-caller abstractions, and the hygiene rules of always-on base.md. Tier is design per registries/models.json work type hard-debugging, which covers cross-cutting refactor design.

intents.title: Architecture decision
signals: should we use X or Y
intents.note: The decision gets recorded, not just chatted. Tier is most-capable per registries/models.json work type adr — an ADR is a recorded decision with a long half-life, the same class as a spec. Business, career and positioning decisions go to the strategy row instead; this row owns technical X-vs-Y choices.

intents.title: Release notes
intents.note: Stack-agnostic. Build tier rather than cheap: the notes are written against a real diff and a real version boundary, not summarized mechanically.

intents.title: Business / career strategy
signals: what do I learn, in what order
X or Y and I can't decide
intents.note: Five modes over one grounding discipline: every claim traced to a dated web source or a file in this repo, output persisted to docs/strategy/. Technical X-vs-Y stays with the adr row. Tier is most-capable — the same problem-framing class as spec and PRD authoring in registries/models.json.

intents.title: Review / pre-merge
intents.note: The code-review skill is EXTERNAL — provided by the Claude Code environment, not this repo — so there is no skills/code-review/ directory and unqualified-name resolution must exempt it. It is listed unqualified because that is the name the router table and the Skill tool use. If the diff touches auth, input handling, data or LLM surfaces, also dispatch the security-reviewer subagent via the Agent tool; that pass is design tier per registries/models.json work type adversarial-review, while the standards/spec review itself is the build-tier code-review work type.

intents.title: Test writing
intents.note: Hook-mirrored as the routing.json domain `test`, second in the hook precedence chain, so test files route here rather than to their stack domain. Dispatch test-writer (alias ameer) for well-scoped targets.

intents.title: Eval setup
intents.note: Scaffolding a harness against a known shape is build tier. Shares rules/llm-apps.md with the llm row, which this row will usually co-match.

intents.title: Independent verification of high-risk work
signals: release gate needs an independent pass
intents.note: critic (alias vera): adversarial correctness review, read-only, tries to refute the claim that the work is done. Required by rules/gates.md at risk=high; security-reviewer still owns the security lens. risk_floor high is the tier of the work under review — the row's own stated trigger — not of the review pass, which writes nothing. Tier design per registries/models.json work type adversarial-review.

intents.title: Handoff between agents, waves or sessions
intents.note: The row's load target is templates/handoff.md — a repo template, which is neither a rule nor a skill and so has no field of its own here. Required sections: objective, state, gate, risk, decisions, files, evidence, known failures, next step, resume commands. Never hand off with 'continue where you left off'. Cheap tier: the template is filled from state that already exists.

intents.title: Continuous improvement
intents.note: Mines .engineos/archived/, eval failures and integrity failures for patterns with 3 or more occurrences, then proposes rule, skill and registry deltas as a PR. Proposes only; a human merges. Design tier because the output is policy change, not code.

intents.title: Work complete / close the change record
intents.note: Marks the record done, describes what was made, registers files changed and movements, and moves the record from .engineos/changes/ to .engineos/archived/. Clears the unrecorded-changes flag the Stop hook record-verify.sh enforces.

intents.title: Claiming done / complete / fixed; spec archived / feature shipped
intents.note: Evidence before assertion, always. For spec-archive and ship cases: lint, typecheck, build and an API/Web startup check, output shown, with a fix loop until clean before reporting done. The Stop hooks stop-verify.sh and record-verify.sh are the automated half — they gate on scoped lint/typecheck/tests and on an unrecorded change record — and they cover the Validation gate only, never the Release gate.

intents.title: Ambiguous or multi-agent request needing a dispatch plan
intents.note: The router agent runs scripts/kernel.sh route-escalate and risk FIRST and reasons only about the residue: intent tiebreaks the notes do not settle mechanically, scope decomposition against real files, and wave grouping. It returns a dispatch plan; it never dispatches and never edits. Tier is design per registries/models.json work type architecture, which covers task decomposition and fan-out planning. The deterministic path needs no agent at all — hooks/route-advisor.sh emits the kernel's answer directly when route-escalate reports escalate=false.
